⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: this test's name documents a reset behavior that is neither implemented nor tested**

The test is named *"a rework lap between polish laps resets the budget (not consecutive polish)"*, but its body tests **same-head dedup** (two entries for `HEAD_A` → not exhausted for `HEAD_B`). A reset does not exist anywhere: `instabilityBudgetExhausted` (`js/common/polishLap.js:118-131`) counts **distinct heads over the PR's lifetime** and never resets — there is no interleave detection (the marker payload carries no `kind`; the in-test comment even admits "the interleave … is exercised by the dedup path instead").

Divergence from the documented contract — the module header (`polishLap.js:22-24`) promises *"2 consecutive polish laps on consecutive heads exhaust the instability budget"*, i.e. a **consecutive** bound, and the test name promises the corresponding reset. The implementation is a **lifetime cap**: after any 2 polish laps on 2 distinct heads — even with a real rework lap (or weeks of human work) in between — polish is permanently off for that PR and every later suggestion-only round falls to triage.

The direction is fail-safe (triage still resolves the threads, nothing wedges), so this is not blocking — but in this repo docs + tests are the contract surface, and a test whose name asserts behavior the code does not have will mislead the next maintainer precisely when they tune the budget.

Resolve one way:

1. **Implement the documented semantics**: record the lap kind in the marker payload (`kind: 'polish'`) and treat a non-polish dispatch between two polish laps as breaking consecutiveness (resetting the budget); then make this test actually construct that interleave, or
2. **Document the lifetime cap**: reword the `polishLap.js` header ("at most `INSTABILITY_BUDGET` distinct heads per PR, lifetime — never resets") and rename this test to what it pins ("duplicate head entries collapse — one lap per head"), which its own assertion message already says.

comments.body:
💡 severity: SUGGESTION —
💡 **SUGGESTION: the doc line names the disposition tag with the other spelling (`deferred` vs the canonical `defered`)**

This header says threads are tagged `deferred: #ledger` (two r's). The machine-parsed literal this module's deferrals actually close with is **`defered`** (one r) — `reviewDispositions.js` `TAGS = ['fixed', 'wontfix', 'duplicate', 'defered']`, canonicalized deliberately per the test pin in `test_reviewDispositions.js:70` ("the epic spells it defered (one r)"), and the ack the executor posts renders `defered: <id>`.

The earlier review asked to rename the code literal to `deferred`; the author instead pinned one-r as canonical (a fair call I'm not re-litigating). The residual wart is **inside this new file**: a maintainer grepping the producer doc (`deferred:`) finds this line but not the parser, and grepping the code literal (`defered:`) misses the doc — exactly the cross-ledger tag-grep failure mode the previous round warned about, now between a file's docs and its own tag.

Fix: change this line to `tagging 'defered: <ledger-id>'` (one r, matching `TAGS`), or add "(spelled `defered` — see reviewDispositions.TAGS)" so both spellings resolve to the same place.

Also: the tag carries the **ledger finding id**, not a `#ledger` reference — `<id>` is the accurate shape (`buildThreadAckReply` → `tagLine` → `defered: 9f2c01ab`).

This added line duplicates the existing `latestVerdictForHead: latestVerdictForHead,` entry already present ~4 lines above (pre-existing on `main`). Duplicate identical keys are runtime-harmless (the later one wins; same value), but they're diff noise and a future edit to one of the two entries will silently be shadowed by the other.

comments.author: ajaxspace
comments.body:
Pre-merge spec review (vs #1352 + epic #1328 §5):

**All five scope points verified in the diff** ✅
1. Polish lap — `polishLap.js`: bounded (single commit, ≤ 6 threads, once per head), polish-tier-only, dispatched on approved BLOCKED heads.
2. Instability budget — `instabilityBudgetExhausted(laps, headSha)`: 2 consecutive polish laps on consecutive heads exhaust polishing → triage-resolve + digest. Cross-head bound as specced, with tests.
3. Triage beyond BLOCKED — dispatch on approved heads, machine-owned threads via the gh-728 machineAuthor parse, policy gate decides closable tiers, `wontfix`/defer dispositions machine-stamped, evidence never rewritten.
4. Ledger reuse — `ledgerCore.js` extraction with the shared batched-sweep trigger (open ≥ 10 OR oldest ≥ 30 days → ONE sweep leg); `reviewDebtLedger.js` as a second consumer alongside the TC-side singleton. Exactly the §5-G economics.
5. `reconcileDecision` — open nits stay ("the polish lap owns them — nits never hold labels"); nit census removed from the AC3 exception list.
Plus the dry-run evidence runner (`scripts/dry-run-disposition-loop.js`, in-memory scripted provider, non-production banner).

**One must-fix finding (small, mechanical):**

The review-side disposition tag literal is spelled **`defered`** (reviewDispositions.js `tag: 'defered'`, the summary line `', defered ' + out.defered`, and the test assertion) while the TC-side maintenance-ledger tag is spelled **`deferred`** (`deferred: #ledger` — this PR's own docs reference it). Two spellings for the same concept in one codebase means tag-greps and any future cross-ledger matching will silently miss one side. Please rename the review-side literal to `deferred` (code + tests + marker text) — the rework round for docs-freshness is a natural vehicle.

**Blocking check:** `docs-freshness` FAILURE — the `instructions/pr_rework/general_guidelines.md` change needs the generated docs refreshed (`docs/agents/generated/*`), otherwise the PR stays BLOCKED and unmergeable.

Both are small; everything else is approve-quality.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: Scope (disposition loop: opportunistic pickup, triage beyond BLOCKED, bounded polish lap, review ledger) is faithfully implemented and well-tested, but one blocking bug must be fixed before merge.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 **BLOCKING** — `js/common/smProvider.js:1037`: `postPrComment` never invalidates the memoized `prVerdicts` comment cache (`ioCacheDrop`), so `deferThreadToLedger`'s per-thread read→append→post loop rebuilds each marker from the stale pre-tick base; the last marker wins and every earlier `defered` finding silently vanishes from the ledger (AC1's 4-deferral tick leaves 1 finding). Data loss; the dry-run masks it (its scripted provider accumulates comments live; production serves a memoized snapshot).
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — `js/unit-tests/test_polishLap.js:166`: the test named "a rework lap … resets the budget" tests same-head dedup instead; no reset exists — `instabilityBudgetExhausted` is a lifetime distinct-head cap, not the documented consecutive-head bound (`polishLap.js:22-24`). Fail-safe direction, but docs/tests assert semantics the code doesn't implement.
- 💡 `js/common/reviewDebtLedger.js:5` — doc line spells the tag `defered` while the canonical machine-parsed literal is `defered` (`reviewDispositions.js` TAGS); tag-greps miss one side.
- 💡 `js/common/smProvider.js:1029` — comment misdescribes the gitlab twin (primitives are absent, which is what fails closed; a literal no-op implementation would fail deferral OPEN).
- 🪶 `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js:857` — duplicate `latestVerdictForHead` export key (pre-existing entry at :853).
- Digest: `machineSmAgent.js:521` logs `issue.number` instead of normalized `issueNo` · `machineSmAgent.js:478-489` duplicated counter shape + dead `duplicate` counter · 29 added lines carry trailing whitespace.

**Verified fixed from the previous round**: docs-freshness — generators re-run on this head, `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated snapshots` clean. Suite green (8557 passed; the single local failure is this sandbox's `FA_SESSION_ROOT` leak, reproducing identically on `origin/main`). Dry-run replays exit 0.

**Next Steps**:
1. Add `ioCacheDrop(owner, repo, 'prVerdicts', String(prNumber))` to `postPrComment` (or carry the running ledger across the deferral loop) + a regression test serving a memoized snapshot with ≥2 deferrals.
2. Implement the budget reset (lap `kind` in the marker + interleave detection) or reword the header/test to the lifetime-cap semantics.
3. Apply the two suggestion-level doc corrections and drop the duplicated export key.
